title: Mobilising Private Capital and National Roadmaps
summary: Brings the programme together by examining blended finance, public development banks and other tools to crowd in private capital, and how to build a national sustainable finance roadmap.
contentGaps: Written as part of a programme: Aim and Purpose is the module's one-line description; audience, prior knowledge and core reading come from the programme

sections.Aim and Purpose: Brings the programme together by examining blended finance, public development banks and other tools to crowd in private capital, and how to build a national sustainable finance roadmap.
Learning Objectives: Evaluate blended finance, guarantees and green investment banks
Prioritise policy measures for the national context and sequence them
Produce a national sustainable finance roadmap
Syllabus: Blended finance, guarantees and first-loss structures
Public development banks, green investment banks and country platforms
Governance of a roadmap: ministries, regulators and industry
Workshop: a national sustainable finance roadmap
Intended Audience: Officials in finance, environment and climate ministries developing sustainable finance and green growth policy
Debt management office staff and public agencies involved in green bond issuance and climate finance
Legislative drafters, legal advisers and parliamentary committee staff working on sustainability disclosure or climate legislation
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Some familiarity with financial services, climate or economic policy is helpful. No technical background in sustainability reporting or climate science is required.
Core Reading: ISSB (2023), IFRS S1 General Requirements for Disclosure of Sustainability-related Financial Information and IFRS S2 Climate-related Disclosures
G20 Sustainable Finance Working Group (2021), G20 Sustainable Finance Roadmap
FSB (2021), FSB Roadmap for Addressing Climate-Related Financial Risks
NGFS (2019), A Call for Action: Climate Change as a Source of Financial Risk
IOSCO (2021), Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) Ratings and Data Products Providers: Final Report
